title: Build it: Acceleration
summary: Implement the module's core functions and make its unit tests pass.

blocks.md: Time to write the code. The file `acceleration.py` contains the whole module, with 7 core parts replaced by `raise NotImplementedError`. Each `TODO(n)` sits under a docstring that says exactly what to build. The tests are the module's own `test_unit_*` functions; run them as often as you like and watch them turn green one by one.

blocks.title: How to work
blocks.md: Open the editor below (or the file in your own editor), fill in one TODO, press **Run tests**, read the first failure, repeat. Earlier TinyTorch modules are already provided as a finished package, so you only write this module.

blocks.title: Implement acceleration
blocks.goal: Fill in the 7 TODO parts of `acceleration.py` so that every unit test passes.
blocks.behavior: Each `TODO(n)` replaces code described by the docstring right above it. The tests (`test_unit_vectorized_matmul`, `test_unit_fused_gelu`, `test_unit_fusion_speedup`, `test_unit_tiled_matmul`, `test_unit_im2col`, `test_unit_im2col_conv2d`, `test_unit_col2im`, `test_unit_im2col_conv2d_function`) call your functions with small tensors and compare the results with the expected values.
hints: Read the docstring above each TODO: it lists the inputs, outputs and an example.
Most parts are a few lines of NumPy on `self.data` wrapped back into a `Tensor`.
Run the tests after each TODO: the failing test's name tells you which function to look at.
blocks.solution_explain: The reference solution is the original TinyTorch implementation of this module.

points: You implemented the acceleration module and its tests pass.
Later modules import exactly this code, the same way PyTorch builds on its tensor core.
